messages.body_plain:
Hi statnet list, Aditya,

As I've already run into this error and it took some reading to find out where it came from, I'll share this here. It could be useful to anyone running jobs on a cluster.
Note that it is not specific to ERGM libraries, but rather to the Rscript call.
See ?Rscript:
"--default-packages=list
where list is a comma-separated list of package names or NULL. Sets the environment variable R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES which determines the packages loaded on startup. The default for Rscript omits methods as it takes about 60% of the startup time."

The function being called during the summary ends up calling findFunction, which has not been loaded since the "methods" library hasn't been loaded.
Quick fix is to load it by hand at the beginning of your file.R with library(methods)

Hope that helps,
Thomas

From: MARTA ROCCHI <marta.rocchi@studenti.unipr.it>
Date: Fri, Nov 6, 2015 at 8:38 AM
Subject: Multiplicative Attribute Graph model for SNA_from Italy
To: mheaney@umich.edu


Dear Mr. Heaney,

I'm an italian PhD student in "Evolutionary Biology and Ecology".
I'm interested in network research, in particular in the study of
social-ecological system (SES) with R.

After reading "*Heaney, M. T. (2014). Intro to Social Network Computing
with R*." I've decided to write this email.

I'm trying to study a fisher community coupled with a marine food web.
I need to build a social network, but I have information only about nodes
attributes (nothing about links).
I've read about Multiplicative Attribute Graph model (I attached the
paper): The Multiplicative Attribute Graphs model (MAG) is a class of
generative models for networks with node attributes. MAG combines
categorical node attributes with their affinities to compute the
probability of a link.

Do you know if this method is already implemented with R? or do you know
other methods to bulid up a social network only from nodes attributes
(i.e., in which someone can detect the probability of a link accoring to a
subset of nodes attribute) with R?

Thank you in advance for any help you might be able to provide.

Sincerely,

Marta Rocchi

messages.body_plain:
Hi Marta,

The statnet tools (and the MAG methods you sent) are designed to estimate 
models from link data -- nodal attributes can be part of the model, but 
nodal attributes alone can not be used to specify a network model in the 
absence data on the links.

Statnet tools can also be used to estimate/simulate networks from target 
statistics -- summary statistics on the links like the number of links, 
the number of links between nodes of different types, the number of closed 
triads, etc.  But there, too, you would need data on the links.

If you don't have data on links, how do you propose to understand your 
data as a network?


best,
Martina

Dear statnet community,

You may already have noticed, but we wanted to let you know that the 
statnet team (finally!) released an update to the statnet "meta package" 
this week which will trigger updates  updates to many of the constituent

Temporal Social Network Analysis

For additional information about the updates, please see the news file 
for each of the packages:


ergm 3.5.1 (2015-20-24)

Hi all,

I am trying to assess model fit for models with some coefficients fixed to
-infinity because their statistics are unobserved. If I understand
correctly, that means deviance and log-likelihood aren?t calculable, so I
can?t use xIC.

In older versions of statnet, mcmc.diagnostics returned a joint p-value
comparing the observed statistics to the distribution from simulations. Now
there?s a message about using gof for this functionality, but I can?t find
that statistic: An assessment of the probability that the observed graph?s
statistics are drawn from a different population than the simulated
graph?s. Using gof(m, GOF = ~model) provides a p-value for each univariate
distribution, but I can?t find one for the joint distribution.

To make things a little trickier, I would like to provide a set of
statistics rather than using the model?s and unfortunately they are not in
the list of supported GOF statistics. My workaround is to simulate from the
model and compare the observed statistics to those from simulations, but
I?m not sure about how to make that comparison (currently comparing the
observed statistics to a multivariate normal distribution constructed from
the simulations), so I?m wondering how mcmc.diagnostics used to do that and
if there might be built-in functionality that could help.

Thanks,

Michael

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Comparing observed to simulated networks on arbitrary statistics
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Comparing observed to simulated networks on arbitrary statistics
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Michael -

There are many ways to make such comparisons, although the most direct 
is to examine the quantiles of the observed graph statistics in the 
distribution of simulated statistics under your proposed model.  Testing 
a joint hypothesis is more complex, and will depend on how the 
hypothesis is defined; a good example is the classic omnibus triad 
census test, of which you can find a discussion in Wasserman and Faust 
(1994).  (One need not use Gaussian approximations in a modern setting: 
one can just simulate the distribution of the test statistic under one's 
proposed model.)  If you want a more elaborate approach, you could also 
consider the quantile modeling methods in Butts (Sociological 
Methodology, 2011); see the comments in section 5.1 about using a 
general probability model (rather than a CUG model) to produce reference 
quantiles.  I would not recommend this for basic hypothesis testing, but 
the approach can be useful in meta-analytic settings where one has 
multiple networks from a possibly heterogeneous population.

Hope that helps,

-Carter

On Wed, 18 Nov 2015, Michael Levy wrote:

>       Hi all,
>
>       I am trying to assess model fit for models with some coefficients fixed to -infinity because their
>       statistics are unobserved. If I understand correctly, that means deviance and log-likelihood aren?t
>       calculable, so I can?t use xIC.

Michael -- just to make sure, when you say "unobserved", do you mean that 
these stats take the value 0 in your data, or do you mean that you do not 
observe the value of these stats in your data (e.g., if you have an 
unlabeled egocentric sample, you won't observe triads).

If you set a coef to -inf, the model is not agnostic to the configuration 
represented by the statistics, it effectively prevents the configuration 
from occurring.  So that's the appropriate thing to do if these statistics 
are known to be 0.  But it's not appropriate if the statistics are simply 
not observed.

best,
mm

messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

I may be missing something in the way I understand the model/implementation
of ERGM.
Reading some documentation and tutorials I see that nodefactor can be used
in order to model the contribution of a nodal attribute to a tie formation.
However, in case of a directed graph - how can I separate the the effect of
a nodal attribute on the incoming edges vs. the outgoing edges.

Here is a toy example: let's consider the famous high school friendship
network and assume it's not an undirected friendship network but a directed
"hitting on" network. Now assume we want to test the hypothesis that guys
are less shy than girls thus they are more likely to be the ones that ask
for a date (a directed edge).

So models like:
rgm(faux.mesa.high ~ edges +  nodefactor("Sex"))

will produce  an estimate for the likelihood of the gender to have an
effect on tie formation, that is to be *involved* in a tie but not on the
the role of the node as a source or a target.

Am I right about it?
Is there a way to use nodefactor (or nodal attributes) in the context of
the direction of the edges?

Thanks a lot!

Oren Tsur
Network Science Institute, Northeastern University

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] representing and estimating a "partial homophily" term
messages.body_plain:
(a second question for the day).

Let's consider the famous high school friendship network. Now assume that
student are taking extra-curricular activities such as clubs. Unlike the
"grade" covariate, assume that a student can be affiliated with more than
one club.
I would like to introduce a term (binary/weighted) that reflects the facts
that two students are members of the same club as I suspect that such a
nodematch increase the likelihood of an edge.

I could have a binary nodal attribute for each club then use nodematch for
each of these attributes but (a) I suspect it will be very inefficient and
(b) I don't care about the specific clubs - I only care about the mutual
membership (this can be viewed as another network N based on mutual
membership where N[i,j] = k where k is the number of clubs i and j share
membership to. In a more simplistic scenario k is a binary attribute
indicating if they share any club membership or not).

Is there a way to introduce such a term into an ERGM model (and represent
it as a node attribute of type list) or that I have to add a separate nodal
attribute for each club and introduce a nodematch("<club>") term for each
club?

An alternative way to think about it whether it is possible to have a term
representing *another network* N2, hypothesizing that a (weighted?) tie in
N2 increases the likelihood of observing a tie in the network in question.

Thanks again!

--
Oren Tsur
Network Science Institute, Northeastern University

On Mon, 23 Nov 2015, Oren Tsur wrote:

>

> extra-curricular activities such as clubs. Unlike the "grade" covariate, assume that a student can be
> affiliated with more than one club.

> of the same club as I suspect that such a nodematch increase the likelihood of an edge. 
> 
> I could have a binary nodal attribute for each club then use nodematch for each of these attributes but
> (a) I suspect it will be very inefficient

since this is a dyad independent effect, the estimation is pretty 
straightforward (essentially the same as logistic regression) so there's 
no real issue of efficiency.

> and (b)? I don't care about the specific clubs - I only care
> about the mutual membership (this can be viewed as another network N based on mutual membership where
> N[i,j] = k where k is the number of clubs i and j share membership to. In a more simplistic scenario k
> is a binary attribute indicating if they share any club membership or not).

i would think you might be more interested in a quantitative measure of 
how many club memberships they have in common.

> Is there a way to introduce such a term into an ERGM model (and represent it as a node attribute of type
> list) or that I have to add a separate nodal attribute for each club and introduce a nodematch("<club>")
> term for each club?

you can create a dyad covariate that takes the value 1 if they share any 
club memberships, but you'll need to do this outside of the ergm call. 
it's a data processing step that will use the utilities in R and the 
network package.

> An alternative way to think about it whether it is possible to have a term representing *another
> network* N2, hypothesizing that a (weighted?) tie in N2 increases the likelihood of observing a tie in

Hello Statnet Community,

I have a quick question about how the ordering of vertices within network objects can be customized. I need this customization to be able to make certain plots seamlessly later. The vertex names of my network objects are not simply numeric, they are character strings that identify individuals, and indicators of their participation in a select group are encoded in these names.

I am not able to customize this ordering. I see that
    net$iel
presents a list of all the vertex id's that each vertex id is linked to. But I am not able to see how I can manipulate the ordering within this list, to fit my needs.

I'd appreciate any help in figuring this problem out.

Many thanks,
Aditya

simple_triplet_matrix or dgCMatrix in Matrix package.? Thanks.



Best,
